fixture.description: parseBoundary documents that a nonexistent local time must be rejected, but parses with a STRICT formatter (which only validates the calendar fields) and then calls atZone(Europe/Paris), which silently shifts 2026-03-29 02:30 (spring-forward gap) to 03:30 instead of rejecting it.

grader.rubric: PASS if the report flags at IMPORTANT or CRITICAL that parseBoundary does not reject nonexistent local times: the STRICT resolver does not catch a DST gap, and LocalDateTime.atZone silently shifts e.g. 02:30 on the Europe/Paris spring-forward date to 03:30, contradicting the documented rejection; fix is to check the round trip (zdt.toLocalDateTime().equals(local)) or use the zone rules' getValidOffsets/ gap detection. FAIL if absent, below IMPORTANT, or if it wrongly claims the STRICT formatter already rejects it.

expected_behavior: Explains that atZone adjusts a gap time forward by the gap length
Suggests a round-trip or ZoneRules validity check
expected_not_behavior: Does NOT claim the strict formatter makes the method safe
